questions.q: Recite «أَطْعَمَهُم مِّن جُوعٍۢ» (106:4) and name the rule.
questions.a: Idgham shafawi: the meems merge with a two-count hum.

questions.q: How many counts of ghunnah in idgham shafawi?
Rule sort (pupil PDF): label 97:4 «رَبِّهِم مِّن», 96:14 «يَعْلَم بِأَنَّ», 106:4 «وَءَامَنَهُم مِّنْ». Today's rota group recites At-Tin 95:1 to 3 to the teacher.
questions.a: Idgham shafawi, ikhfa shafawi, idgham shafawi.

questions.q: Extend: recite Surat Quraysh and point out both idgham shafawi.
questions.a: Both are in 106:4: أَطْعَمَهُم مِّن and وَءَامَنَهُم مِّنْ.

questions.q: Stretch: what is the same and different about «مِّن» after idgham and «ثُمَّ» (95:5)?
questions.a: Both have a meem with shaddah and a two-count ghunnah; in ثُمَّ the shaddah is inside one word.
A) رَبِّهِم مِّن. Meem sakinah before م merges: idgham shafawi. The others are ikhfa and izhar.

questions.q: Think again: Two friends walk through a door at exactly the same time and look like one. How could two meem letters become one sound?
questions.a: The first meem has no vowel, so it joins the second: one meem with shaddah and a two-count hum.
